1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Felsheim for three days. That spring, Anna Weber's older sister had left for Berlin, and since then Anna had been running the village's small apothecary alone.
At nightfall she shut the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone knocked loudly at the door downstairs. A man's voice called, "Is anyone there?"
Outside the door stood a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloody cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need a bandage," Wolf said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred marks do?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oil paper from his jacket. "This letter must be at Steinbach Monastery before the eighteenth of May."
Anna must have been blind: only now did she notice how pale he was.
Still, she didn't take his money and simply said, "Tomorrow morning I'll take you into the mountains."
2: At daybreak they set out. Anna carried a basket on her back with bread, healing herbs, and an old umbrella inside.

Halfway up they met old Hans Becker, who was chopping wood. He set the axe aside and said quietly that yesterday evening three strangers had inquired at the village entrance about an injured young man.
"Take the path, Anna," said Hans Becker. "The main road isn't safe." Anna thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Anna went ahead, placing each step with care. Wolf followed her in silence.
Around noon the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of Steinbach Monastery appeared. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who received the guests at the monastery.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Wolf said to Anna: "I owe you my life." Anna smiled: "Then next time, fix the roof of my apothecary." Wolf stayed at the monastery.
In the evening Anna descended the mountain alone. When she got home, it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
